heading: EXT. DRY SALT FLAT - ABANDONED STAGECOACH CROSSING - DAY

units.text: EXT. DRY SALT FLAT - ABANDONED STAGECOACH CROSSING - DAY
White ground in every direction.
A cracked water trough, a hitching post, and one leaning shed.
CALEB DRUMMOND (40s, sunburned, dusty duster) sits on an upturned bucket, counting out coins onto a flat stone.
His mule DOLLY stands hipshot beside him, one ear back.
Eleven dollars and a button.
units.name: CALEB

units.text: He lifts the button and flicks it away.
You eat more than a church.
units.name: CALEB

units.text: He listens.
Wind.
Nothing else.
He gets up, walks to the trough, and looks into it.
Dry as a Baptist's Sunday. Should've gone north.
units.name: CALEB

units.text: He cups his hands to his mouth and calls out across the flat.
Anybody in that shed, I got a rifle and no patience!
units.name: CALEB

units.text: The shed door creaks.
A figure leans in the shadow.
Caleb levels the rifle.
OLD MARISOL VEGA (70s, black rebozo, a cane carved with snakes) steps into the light, squinting.
She carries a tin cup.
You will scare the water, shouting like that.
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: There's no water.
units.name: CALEB

units.text: Under the third board of the shed. Two feet down. It comes back at noon.
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: Caleb lowers the rifle slowly.
Ma'am, I about shot you.
units.name: CALEB

units.text: Many have wanted to.
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: She offers him the tin cup.
He takes it, turns it over in his hand, then looks at the sun.
Two feet. Third board. Lord help me.
units.name: CALEB

units.text: He tips his hat to her, takes the shovel from the wall, and heads for the shed.
Dolly follows, flicking her tail.
Share with the animal. She has been patient.
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: Always am, ma'am. Always am.
units.name: CALEB
